answer: With a Verified email inbox bound by callback verification with a public binding record, the account is only as strong as its binding: the verified email inbox answers a fresh challenge, the callback verification is recorded, and a public binding record keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. One nadir proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of bindings. No walnut is counted twice and no juniper is skipped: the ledger reconciles every binding.
